adjudication.rationale: In Office365CalendarService.createEvent the code now destructures only the first element of the new array-typed `event.destinationCalendar` (`const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = event.destinationCalendar ?? []`) and builds the POST URL from that (`/me/calendars/${mainHostDestinationCalendar.externalId}/events`). Meanwhile, EventManager was changed to support multiple destination calendars by iterating `for (const destination of event.destinationCalendar)` and calling `createEvent(...)` per destination/credential, but it passes the same `event` object each time (it does not narrow `event.destinationCalendar` to the current `destination`). adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:147 — Untested: when no destinationCalendar entry matches credentialId (e.g. legacy rows with null credentialId) the event silently lands on "primary"

adjudication.rationale: Real issue. In `GoogleCalendarService.createEvent`, the target calendar is now chosen via `calEventRaw.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.credentialId === credentialId)?.externalId`, and then `calendarId: selectedCalendar || "primary"`. If no `destinationCalendar` entry matches the passed `credentialId` (including cases where entries have `credentialId: null/undefined`), `selectedCalendar` becomes `undefined` and the insert silently falls back to the user's `primary` calendar even if a non-primary `externalId` exists in `destinationCalendar`. This behavior change is directly visible in the diff and can misroute events.

Meanwhile, event creation is now credential-specific (`CalendarManager.createEvent` calls `calendar.createEvent(calEvent, credential.id)` and `EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents` loops over `event.destinationCalendar` and creates events per destination/credential), but the Office365 service does not use the credential id (it doesn’t accept it and can’t select the matching destination calendar entry).
